candidate_sources.README.md:
# Workspace drafts with asynchronous acknowledgements

open/edit/close are synchronous. The editor currently submits every edit.
A visit's latest pending text must be submitted exactly once before close or
navigation returns; submission must not wait for network acknowledgement.
Accepted writes belong to the document, survive navigation, and all settle.
Store read exposes the latest accepted draft for immediate reopen; readPersisted
exposes acknowledged data, protected by write revision against late old writes.
The provided transport accepts a write synchronously and returns a Promise.
Its start callback may synchronously open another document, reopen the same
one, hide the editor, or edit that new visit. Acceptance occurs before that hook.
Navigation priority follows call start order: a newer open/close supersedes an
outer navigation that resumes after a save-start callback. Obsolete destinations
must not render. A newly accepted edit must not be erased by old flush cleanup.

A save-status notification may appear only for the current visit's latest edit.
A pending newer edit invalidates an older acknowledgement even before its own
write is submitted. store.write(id,text,owner) round-trips an opaque owner token;
attachSaveStatus supports an owner predicate. Reopening the same document does
not give its new visit ownership of the old visit's acknowledgement.
Do not cancel accepted saves to suppress UI messages. No network failures or
retry policy are included in this fixture; each transport Promise settles once.

The search preview is transient: 40 ms quiet interval, discard pending query
on hide, reusable afterward. It is outside the editor maintenance request.

checkpoints: On every edit, immediately record that visit’s newest owner token and pending text so an older acknowledgement is no longer eligible for save-status display.
At the 120 ms trailing-task callback, retire the pending burst before calling store.write so synchronous transport reentry cannot erase newly queued work.
Before open, close, or dispose returns, synchronously flush the outgoing visit’s latest pending burst without waiting for its transport Promise.
After a save-start callback returns, re-check navigation currency before rendering its destination or clearing state, because nested navigation has priority.
Run the public JavaScript syntax/build checks after an Action; they do not establish business correctness.
forbidden_effects: Do not submit every keystroke individually.
Do not submit stale intermediate text from the same uninterrupted editing burst.
Do not wait for network acknowledgement during open, close, navigation, or dispose.
Do not cancel an accepted store write or prevent its Promise from settling merely to suppress UI output.
Do not allow a late older acknowledgement to overwrite newer persisted data.
Do not render an obsolete destination after a synchronous save-start callback performs newer navigation.
Do not let cleanup of an old flush erase an edit accepted or queued during callback reentry.
Do not let a new visit to the same document claim an old visit’s acknowledgement.
Do not change the adjacent search preview.
lifecycle_identity: Each editor open creates a distinct visit identity, including when reopening the same document.
Each edit creates a new opaque owner token immediately; that token becomes the visit’s latest owner before the delayed write occurs.
The trailing burst retains only the latest text and owner token for that visit.
The owner token supplied to store.write must round-trip unchanged in the acknowledgement event.
A save-status event is eligible only when its document matches, its visit is still current, and its owner is that visit’s latest edit owner.
Accepted writes belong to the document and remain valid independently of the visit that initiated them.

obligations.text: Coalesce editor edits with the existing trailing-task utility using a 120 ms quiet interval.
For one editing burst, submit exactly one store write containing only that burst’s latest text and latest owner token after 120 ms without another edit.
After a burst is submitted, later edits must form new bursts that can each be submitted normally.

If open, close, or dispose retires a visit with pending text, synchronously submit that visit’s latest pending text exactly once before the navigation operation returns, without awaiting acknowledgement.
Preserve immediate invalidation of older save-status acknowledgements: a newer edit becomes the visit’s latest owner as soon as edit is called, even while its write remains delayed.

Preserve store semantics: acceptance precedes the transport callback, read exposes the latest accepted draft, accepted writes settle independently, and revision ordering prevents older acknowledgements from rolling persisted data back.
Preserve navigation reentrancy semantics: navigation begun later from a synchronous transport start callback supersedes an outer open or close, and obsolete destinations must not render.
Preserve visit-scoped save-status ownership so only the current visit’s latest edit may notify status; reopening the same document must not inherit acknowledgement ownership from the prior visit.
Preserve all existing public interfaces and synchronous open/edit/close behavior, and leave search-preview behavior outside the change.

ordering_barriers: An edit’s latest-owner assignment and pending-burst update occur before any older acknowledgement can be accepted for status display.
The 120 ms interval is restarted by each edit in the current burst; submission occurs only after a full quiet interval or an explicit lifecycle flush.
A lifecycle flush submits the outgoing visit’s latest pending burst before open, close, or dispose returns.
Burst state is retired before store.write invokes transport, because transport may synchronously navigate, hide, reopen, or edit.
Acceptance into the store occurs before the transport start hook.
Navigation priority is determined by call start order; an outer navigation that resumes after nested navigation must not overwrite or render over the newer navigation.
Network acknowledgement is not a barrier for navigation completion.
Persisted-data publication is guarded by per-document write revision so late older completion cannot roll data back.
preservation: open, edit, close, and dispose retain their current public signatures and synchronous calling convention.
Opening a document still renders its latest accepted store value immediately when that open remains current.
Closing still retires status observation and renders no document when that close remains current.
Store read continues to expose accepted drafts immediately; readPersisted continues to expose revision-protected acknowledged data.
Every accepted write continues to settle independently.
Save-status notification remains restricted to the current visit’s latest edit.
The existing search preview keeps its 40 ms quiet interval, hide cancellation, and reusability.
The existing trailing-task utility remains reusable for subsequent batches and safe when its work callback enqueues another batch.
scope: Business-code changes are limited to the workspace draft editor’s edit coalescing and the lifecycle handoff needed to preserve existing navigation and save-status behavior.
The existing trailing-task utility is the required coalescing mechanism.
The adjacent search preview, tests, configuration, and public interfaces are outside the requested modification.

triggers: Calling edit(text) while a visit is current starts or refreshes that visit’s trailing save burst.
Reaching 120 ms with no newer edit triggers submission of the burst’s latest text.
Calling open(id), close(), or workspace dispose() while the outgoing visit has a pending burst triggers an immediate flush before the operation returns.
Transport acceptance may synchronously trigger nested open, reopen, close/hide, or edit calls; these are reentrant lifecycle triggers.
Settlement of an accepted transport Promise triggers revision-protected persistence and subscriber notification.
